People's Majlis Committee Minutes

5th Meeting of the Environment and Climate Change Committee

24 June 2026

Venue of the meeting: People's Majlis building (Committee Room 6)
Start time: 11:00

{Presiding: Committee Chair; Member for South Maafannu constituency, Abdulla Rifau}

Remarks from the Chair:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Welcome to the 5th meeting of the People's Majlis Environment and Climate Change Committee, the 5th meeting of this session. The meeting is being held in Committee Room 6. Today's date is 24 June 2026, Wednesday. The time is 11:30. On today's agenda is a discussion of various matters before the Committee. At the last meeting we held, a meeting with us from the Audit Office; before proceeding, I will read out the names of the members present at today's sitting. Myself, Member for South Maafannu constituency Abdulla Rifau; Member for Mulaku constituency Ibrahim Naufal; Member for Central Hulhumale' constituency Abdulla Shazeem; Member for West Maafannu constituency Mohamed Musthafa; Member for Mathiveri constituency Hassan Zareer; Member for Gemanafushi constituency Asadhulla Shihab; Member for South Thinadhoo constituency Mohamed Alsan; Member for Keyodhoo constituency Mohamed Niushad. At the last meeting we held, we discussed that day that the Audit Office had requested a meeting with us. However, the Audit Office has now shared with us in writing the matters they wanted to raise at that meeting, or the information they wanted to share in connection with that meeting. Therefore, having decided to file what was discussed that day on this matter, you can now see the letter they have sent. I would like to add that this letter has also been shared in our WhatsApp group. Yes! For your information, Member for Hithaadhoo constituency Mohamed Siruhaan has joined our meeting. Yes! If any member wishes to put forward any view on this letter or on any other matter, please go ahead. Member for Mathiveri constituency.

Remarks by Member for Mathiveri constituency Hassan Zareer:
Thank you, Chair. What we can see on the screen just now is a paper that the Audit Office sent us in writing about the work they are doing, after we asked to meet with them

[stamp]

Looking through this paper, it also says that they have become a member of an international auditing firm, and of that firm. I believe that, with the Maldives Audit Office working together with these international firms, what we want, particularly since many of the issues in the environment are very sensitive matters. Particularly that, even when auditing, a great many things have to be taken into account. Particularly, being a small island nation and with our entire tourism industry dependent on it, the reality of this country is that our main income-generating resource is the income earned from tourism, which is a natural resource. Therefore, as I said earlier, I believe that when we audit the various environmental issues of this island nation that relate to tourism, that work will be sped up through a link with an international firm. However, I would like to note, with great regret, that many past governments have in reality not worked adequately to find real solutions to the issues in the environment. In that regard, looking through it, I believe that in particular we also need to amend our laws. And some regulations as well; we came to notice this because of various environmental incidents, particularly vessels running aground on reefs and the like, or damage to corals, to reef corals, and this Committee has already been informed before that there are major challenges in collecting for the State the fines imposed for these, or in recovering that money. Therefore, in reality, a very important foundation, or an important aim, of our Environment Committee is to organise our work in a way that protects our natural wealth and also increases our income. Therefore, I would further request that the fines we are imposing, particularly, you know. We always advocate and talk about how large the fine amounts are. I say this because, in reality, not even 5% of the fines imposed has been recovered to date. And when the Audit Office audits for court proceedings and, based on that, often looks to send a case to court

[stamp]

I would also like to note that, under the auditing system currently in place in the Maldives, the audit reports do not identify enough evidence and proof for a case to be sent. Therefore, before concluding my remarks, I request that we begin work, together with government ministries or with the various ministries connected to this Committee, to reduce our fines and penalties to a level we find acceptable, or to a level at which they can actually be collected. I say this because, as I said earlier, under no government, and under none of the governments that have come before, has even 5% of the fines imposed been recovered. In that proportion it has become a very large amount, and it is not even an amount that can be paid. However, that is how it stands under the law. Therefore, I will close my remarks by asking all members to give thought to this matter. Thank you very much, Chair.

Remarks from the Chair:
Does any member wish to express any view on that? Yes! If no member wishes to express any further view, I will close today's committee meeting. Thank you very much.

[stamp]
